key_insight: EvolveNav makes zero-shot object-goal navigation more adaptive by letting the agent improve itself during testing instead of relying on fixed priors. It combines proactive preflection with self-evolving memory so the agent can learn from its own mistakes and reduce repeated errors.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the challenge of Zero-Shot Object-Goal Navigation, where an embodied agent must find a target object without task-specific training. Existing foundation-model-based methods often stay static at test time, causing inefficient exploration, repeated mistakes, and costly trial-and-error behavior.
method: Build an agentic rule memory that extracts actionable navigation knowledge from experience.
Use proactive preflection to anticipate likely mistakes and adjust decisions before acting.
Continuously update memory during test time so the policy self-evolves across navigation episodes.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows a path toward more robust embodied agents that adapt online without retraining. It is especially useful for real-world navigation settings where environments are unfamiliar and static policies quickly become unreliable.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing perception -> preflection -> action -> memory update loop

Trajectory map highlighting repeated errors reduced over time
paper_title: EvolveNav: Proactive Preflection and Self-Evolving Memory for Zero-Shot Object Goal Navigation
paper_authors: Qi Chai, Wenhao Shen, Nanjie Yao, Yue Xia, Kaiyong Zhao
